subject: Refining normal distribution with one data point

messages.author: 6604e12f52408f14
messages.subject: Refining normal distribution with one data point
parts:
Hi

I'm just starting to experiment with Stan and am having trouble with what I think is a simple problem. 

When trying to refine a normal distribution with new data, the attached script works fine if I have two or more new data points (the y variable).  But if there's only one new data point, then I get the attached errors. 

Have I misunderstood something fundamental? Or is there just a type casting issue somewhere that confuses a vector of length 1 with some other data type? If so, perhaps a more informative error message could be introduced for fast mode (the current one complains about length mismatches). 

I do have a copy of Bayesian Data Analysis 2nd ed, so please do feel free to tell me to go read!

Many thanks,
James

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Refining normal distribution with one data point [R scalars vs. arrays]
parts:
Ack. No, it's because (a) we do error checking for shape on the
inputs, and (b) R conflates scalars and implicit arrays of length 1.
So if you do

b <- c(17.2);

then R doesn't know if b is a length-1 array or a scalar. The above
produces the same result in b as

b <- 17.2;

Jiqiang provides a workaround here:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/d-R7J6MldkQ

Bottom line is that instead of

"b" = b

in a list, you need to use the array() function

"b" = array(b, dim=length(b))

to convince R that the value for "b" in the list is an array.

Yet another gotcha we need to somehow call out in the doc
without being too distracting.

- Bob
